story: Goldman Sachs is spending $100M to shave milliseconds off stock trades
text: Tom Scott did a nice video [1] on IEX's setup with 38 miles of fiber to add enough latency as a mechanism of fairness. Purportedly, this benefits all exchanges after it was successfully deployed. It seems like the incentives are not there for larger, more established exchanges to implement such blanket latency. So, firms like GS see a benefit to this kind of investment. [1] [VIDEO]

story: Companies Pitch Shortwave Radio to Shave Milliseconds Off Trades
text: The IEX stock exchange uses fibre to introduce a fixed delay - [LINK] "This 350 microsecond delay adds a round-trip delay of 0.0007 seconds and is designed to negate the certain speed advantages utilized by some high-frequency trader" I watched this short video about it too - [VIDEO]
Tom Scott made a short video about these cables: [VIDEO] 61 kilometres of fibre-optics for a 350 microsecond delay.

story: Intruder at the top of the 20 meter amateur band?
text: Do exchanges like HF traders? I know HF traders themselves justify their own existence by claiming they provide liquidity to the markets, but I've always just sort-of rolled my eyes at that. They only extract value and provide none, in my opinion, tax the profits heavily. I think every exchange should pad each order by a random number between 0 and 250ms, it would take care of it. story: Commercial Interests Petition FCC for High Power Allocation on Shortwave
text: There's actually an exchange that did this. In order to avoid software problems that would negate the slowing, they actually plugged their servers into a giant box full of fiber optic cable. If someone manages to get past that, then they don't have an HFT firm, they have a time machine. [VIDEO]
